# Introduction


I am slowly converting towards learning Python for understanding the newer AI / Machine learning devevelopemtn, and for that I thought it would be best to finally start learning Positron at the same time. Although I have had experience with using Visual Studio code when I was attempting to learning Game Development and conducting some small tracking programmes using the `cv2` library. 

However, I wanted to fully implement Quarto and with the help of Positron and 




Positron uses a workspace environment with features that highly resemble Visual Studio code's environemtn of panes, command palette and have less of an "R-Native" feel to it. Nonetheless, to feel uncomfortable is an initial state that is required before learning something that is new. Additionally, Rstudio uses `.Rproj` files to define projects through


Technical & Feature Challenges

- Environment & Package Management

RStudio integrates smoothly with .libPaths() and package installs. In Positron, you may need to manage environments differently (e.g., using renv, virtual environments, or external tools), which can feel more manual.


Debugger & Interactive Features

RStudio has a very polished R debugger and environment viewer.
Positron is still maturing in this area — some of the tools you rely on may not yet be fully implemented.




RStudio → Positron transition feels like: moving from a specialized, purpose-built IDE to a more general-purpose, flexible coding environment.

Main challenges: losing RStudio’s polished R-specific workflow while gaining broader language flexibility.
